solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Avoid more bizarre film genre (4,5)

indicators.note: bizarre = weird, so the letters come out in a strange order

annotation.surface: Someone vows to steer clear of stranger kinds of cinema.
annotation.walkthrough: 'More bizarre' reads as a comparative adjective, but 'more' belongs with 'Avoid' as fodder and 'bizarre' alone does the stirring.
annotation.definitionFit: A road movie is a film genre built around a journey, like Easy Rider or Thelma & Louise.

entries.clue: Regularly reapplied for fleet (5)

indicators.note: regularly = at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

annotation.surface: Paint or polish is put on again and again to keep a fleet of ships looking smart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a noun, a group of ships, but here it is the adjective meaning swift.
annotation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means fast-moving, as in 'fleet of foot', which is what rapid means.

entries.clue: China kept in check by America and Nato? (7)

indicators.note: something kept in check is held in, so CRONY is held inside AM

blocks.note: Am. is the standard abbreviation for America
china = mate in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate), so a crony

annotation.surface: A geopolitical line: China being contained by the United States and its NATO allies.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes China the country; it is Cockney rhyming slang, 'china plate' for mate. The question mark flags that NATO is only one example of an acronym.
annotation.definitionFit: NATO is formed from the initials of North Atlantic Treaty Organization and spoken as a word, so it is an acronym.

entries.clue: Measuring chaps’ allotment after second of surveys (11)

indicators.note: takes the second letter of the next word
RATION is placed after the U

blocks.note: a ration is an allotted share

annotation.surface: Surveyors measure out a plot of land for some men after a survey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Allotment' suggests a British garden plot, which fits the surveying picture; here it is simply an allotted share, a ration.
annotation.definitionFit: Mensuration is the act or science of measuring, especially lengths, areas and volumes.

entries.clue: Give bear nuts and waffle (8)

indicators.note: nuts = crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: A zookeeper's instruction to feed the bear nuts and a waffle.
annotation.walkthrough: Nuts and waffle both look like food for the bear; 'nuts' is the anagram signal and 'waffle' is the definition, meaning wordy talk.
annotation.definitionFit: Waffle is lengthy talk with little content, which is exactly verbiage.

entries.clue: Crude foxhole close to enemy (6)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a fox's den is called its earth

annotation.surface: A soldier's rough dugout lies right near the enemy lines.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a military foxhole; the wordplay wants a real fox's hole, which is called an earth.
annotation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and unrefined, so crude.

entries.clue: Some of Giuseppe’s tomato sauce (5)

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used, a run from inside the words

annotation.surface: An Italian cook named Giuseppe makes a tomato sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: The Italian setting makes 'tomato sauce' look like one phrase; the answer is a different Italian sauce, and it sits across the apostrophe.
annotation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, garlic, pine nuts and cheese.

entries.clue: Pulse beginning to alter after exercise (3)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the next word
after = following in sequence, so A follows PE in the across reading order

annotation.surface: A doctor notes that the heart rate starts to change after a workout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' plays the heartbeat after exercise; it is the other sense, an edible seed such as a pea, bean or lentil.
annotation.definitionFit: A pulse is the edible seed of a legume, and the pea is one.

entries.clue: Tot reportedly smelt extremely rank at first (7)

indicators.note: reportedly = as it is said, so what you hear is used
takes the first letters of the preceding words

blocks.note: smelt = sniffed, which is said like SNIFT
the first letters of Extremely Rank

annotation.surface: A gossip says a small child smelt awful to begin with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler, and the smell seems to be a nappy; it is a small measure of spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: A snifter is a small drink of spirits, which is a tot.

entries.clue: Agreed over crucial day on Love Island (4-5)

blocks.note: o = over, as on a cricket scorecard
the pieces are joined on to one another
love = nil = O, as in tennis scoring
a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys

annotation.surface: Contestants on the TV dating show Love Island agree terms on a big day.
annotation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British reality dating show, which makes the words look like one title. Split, love is zero and an island is a key.
annotation.definitionFit: Okey-dokey is a jokey way of saying 'agreed' or 'all right'.

entries.clue: Other half of ripped carpet put back (7)

indicators.note: put back = turned round so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to carpet someone is to reprimand them, to rap them

annotation.surface: Half of a torn rug is laid back in place.
annotation.walkthrough: The rug picture makes 'carpet' a noun; it is the verb meaning to tell off, which gives RAP.
annotation.definitionFit: Your other half is your spouse or partner.

entries.clue: Come to see lies are bad (7)

indicators.note: bad = gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A moral lesson: someone comes to understand that lying is wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a sermon on honesty, so 'bad' reads as moral judgement rather than as an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: coming to see a truth is grasping it at last, the sense of 'see' as understand rather than look.

entries.clue: Stop cycling, and retreat (3)

indicators.note: cycling = going round, so the last letter moves round to the front

blocks.note: end = stop; cycling moves the D to the front

annotation.surface: A cyclist gives up riding and heads back home.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes cycling a bike ride; here it means rotating the letters of END.
annotation.definitionFit: A den is a private room or hideaway, a retreat.

entries.clue: Desert Frank after change of heart (11)

indicators.note: the heart is the middle letter, and it is changed

blocks.note: the middle letter of the 11, the sixth, I, becomes A

annotation.surface: A deserter named Frank has second thoughts about leaving.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desert' and 'Frank' look like a verb and a man's name; one is an adjective, the other the adjective frank.
annotation.definitionFit: Desert as an adjective, as in 'desert island', describes a place where nobody lives.

entries.clue: Crazy family’s potential sources of embarrassment (6,5)

annotation.surface: A mad family could be the cause of shame to anyone related to them.
annotation.walkthrough: The word break in the answer falls one letter away from the break in the wordplay, which is what hides it.
annotation.definitionFit: In British usage a banana skin is a pitfall likely to cause public embarrassment, as a banana peel makes you slip.

entries.clue: Lobby group and Liberal refused to agree (8)

indicators.note: the L is refused, turned away, so it is taken out

blocks.note: a camp is a faction, a group
to align = to agree; with the L refused it is AIGN

annotation.surface: A pressure group and a Liberal politician fail to reach agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lobby group' reads as one phrase, but 'Lobby' alone is the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: lobbying politicians means pressing them to back a cause, organised effort for change.

entries.clue: Shoved chaps into hole in wall (9)

indicators.note: shoved = pushed about, so the letters are knocked out of order

annotation.surface: Some men are pushed through a gap in a wall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hole in the wall' is British slang for a cash machine, an ATM set into a bank's outside wall.
annotation.definitionFit: A cashpoint is a British cash machine, colloquially a hole in the wall.

entries.clue: Batty woman in Alaska is trainspotter (6)

indicators.note: in = inside, so the woman sits within the state's letters

blocks.note: AK = Alaska, its US state code
Nora Batty, a character in Last of the Summer Wine

annotation.surface: A slightly mad woman in Alaska turns out to be a railway enthusiast.
annotation.walkthrough: Nora Batty is the wrinkled-stockinged battleaxe of the long-running British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine; 'Batty' is her surname, not a comment on her sanity.
annotation.definitionFit: In Britain an anorak is an obsessive hobbyist, the trainspotter being the stock example, after the coats they wear.

entries.clue: Old lady keeping gold only in vaults (8)

indicators.note: MA keeps AU and SOLE inside it

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: An elderly woman stores her gold in bank vaults and nowhere else.
annotation.walkthrough: The bank vault picture hides the other sense: burial vaults, the tombs.
annotation.definitionFit: Mausolea, the Latin plural of mausoleum, are grand tombs, burial vaults.

entries.clue: Still elated after departure of first couple (6)

indicators.note: the first two letters leave the word

blocks.note: elated = overjoyed, a synonym whose first two letters then leave

annotation.surface: Someone remains happy after the first pair of guests leave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still elated' reads as 'still happy'; 'Still' is the adjective meaning motionless.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'still' as an adjective describes something motionless, the sense in 'still water'.

entries.clue: Settle in open country south of Arabia (7)

indicators.note: in a down answer, below: RANGE comes beneath AR

blocks.note: Ar. = Arabian or Arabic, the dictionary abbreviation
a range is open grazing land

annotation.surface: Nomads make a home on open land south of Arabia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Settle in' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'in' is just the link.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: settling a date or a deal means fixing its details, putting things in order.

entries.clue: Caught friend inhaling a Senior Service in a lascivious way (8)

indicators.note: breathing in, so A RN goes inside

blocks.note: c = caught on a cricket scorecard
the Royal Navy, RN, is Britain's senior service

annotation.surface: A friend is caught smoking a Senior Service cigarette in a lewd manner.
annotation.walkthrough: Senior Service is also a British cigarette brand, which is why a friend is 'inhaling' it; the Royal Navy is called the senior service as the oldest armed force.
annotation.definitionFit: Carnally means sensually, in a fleshly or lustful way.

entries.clue: Way to eat Indian spinach dish (7)

indicators.note: LANE eats SAG, taking it inside

blocks.note: sag or saag is the Hindi word for spinach, as in sag aloo

annotation.surface: A way of eating an Indian spinach curry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Indian spinach dish' reads as one curry; the dish is Italian.
annotation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked pasta dish.

entries.clue: Singer and hubby periodically adopted cute kid (6)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

annotation.surface: A celebrity singer and her husband adopt an adorable child.
annotation.walkthrough: The celebrity-adoption story makes 'cute kid' part of the headline, and it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angelic-looking child.

entries.clue: Bracket mum or dad with male sibling (11)

annotation.surface: A form groups a parent together with a son or brother.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Male sibling' reads naturally as brother, but the two words work separately, and the sibling is a sister.
annotation.definitionFit: A parenthesis is one of a pair of round brackets.

entries.clue: Overheard a certain amount (3)

indicators.note: what is overheard is what you hear, so the sound is used

blocks.note: some = a certain, as in 'some person'

annotation.surface: Eavesdropping picks up a fair bit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A certain amount' reads as one phrase; 'a certain' is SOME, which is said like SUM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, most often of money: 'a large sum' is a large quantity of cash.

entries.clue: Fur coats seen originally in ex-Soviet city (5)

indicators.note: MINK coats the S, wrapping round it
at the origin, so the first letter

annotation.surface: Fur coats were on show in a former Soviet city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fur coats' looks like a noun phrase; 'coats' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Minsk, capital of Belarus, was a Soviet city until 1991.

entries.clue: One clobbered senior — it clears the air (7)

indicators.note: clobbered = battered, so the letters are knocked about

annotation.surface: Someone beat up an older person, and it settles the argument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clears the air' sounds like settling a row after the clobbering; it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: An ioniser charges air particles to remove dust and pollutants, clearing the air.

entries.clue: Blue heads of Smurfs are delightful (3)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letters of Smurfs Are Delightful

annotation.surface: A fan says the little blue cartoon Smurfs are lovely.
annotation.walkthrough: Smurfs are famously blue, which makes 'Blue' look like a description of them.
annotation.definitionFit: Blue means sad, feeling low.

entries.clue: Confinement at home after case of lousy liquor (5-2)

indicators.note: the case is the outside, so the first and last letters
after = following, so the home word follows the lousy letters

annotation.surface: Someone is stuck at home after a crate of cheap booze.
annotation.walkthrough: The drinking picture makes confinement sound like being housebound; it is the old word for childbirth.
annotation.definitionFit: Lying-in is the old term for the period of rest after childbirth, known as confinement.

entries.clue: Daughter on covers of Tatler and European Vogue (5)

indicators.note: the covers are the outside, so the first and last letters
in an across clue, D goes on after the rest

blocks.note: the outer letters of EuropeaN, also covered

annotation.surface: A daughter appears on the covers of two fashion magazines.
annotation.walkthrough: Tatler and Vogue are both glossy magazines, so Vogue looks like a title; it is the definition, fashion. 'Covers of' serves both Tatler and European.
annotation.definitionFit: Vogue means the prevailing fashion, a trend.

entries.clue: Players kiss cheek (5,4)

blocks.note: the brass are the players of brass instruments in an orchestra

annotation.surface: Actors kiss each other on the cheek.
annotation.walkthrough: The stage-kiss picture makes 'cheek' a face; it is impudence.
annotation.definitionFit: Brass neck is British slang for nerve or effrontery, which is cheek.
